sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Adams County, Washington?
sections.html:
The Adams County Treasurer bills and collects property tax, and the Assessor sets the values the bill is built on. The Treasurer's page says the 2026 tax statements were mailed on March 13, 2026. The Assessor's office takes exemption and valuation questions at 509-659-3200.

The Treasurer does more than collect the annual bill. The office also acts as the Department of Revenue's agent for the real estate excise tax on property transfers, and it runs the foreclosure process on parcels that fall three years behind. Statements for each tax year should reach owners on or before March 15 under RCW 84.56.020, provided the levy certifications arrive on time.

sections.h2: What is Adams County like for a property owner?
sections.html:
Adams County is a wheat and irrigated farming county in eastern Washington, about 1,925 square miles of land with roughly 11 people per square mile. Ritzville is the county seat, in the northeast corner where Interstate 90 meets U.S. 395, and Othello in the southwest is the largest city. Hatton, Lind and Washtucna are the towns. Lincoln County lies to the north, Whitman to the east, Franklin to the south and Grant to the west.

The county was carved out of Whitman County in November 1883. By 1904 Ritzville had become the largest initial wheat shipping point in the country, and dryland farmers left fields fallow in alternate years to hold moisture. The federal Columbia Basin Project, approved in 1943, reached the county in 1946 with the East Low Canal and Potholes East Canal, and irrigated crops pushed population up by about 12,500 between 1940 and 2010. The present art-deco courthouse in Ritzville dates from 1940.

Census figures show 21,488 residents in July 2025 and 7,220 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the median value of an owner-occupied home was $273,300, 69.3 percent of homes were owner-occupied and median household income was $66,136. Only 33 building permits were issued in 2025, so the housing stock turns over slowly and many sales involve farm parcels, older homes or inherited property.

sections.h2: When are Adams County property taxes due, and what does late payment cost?
sections.html:
The full tax is due by April 30, and a bill over $50 can be split, with half due April 30 and the rest by October 31. The second half for 2026 came due on October 31, so any unpaid second half is now delinquent. Interest follows the schedule in RCW 84.56.020 and is applied to the full year's tax, not just the late half.

ItemRuleSource
StatementsDue out by March 15; 2026 statements mailed March 13RCW 84.56.020; Treasurer

Interest, house or other residence of four units or fewer9 percent a year, no penaltiesRCW 84.56.020

Mail with no readable postmark is still on time if the Treasurer receives it within three business days of the deadline. Ask the Treasurer's office for a current payoff amount, because interest is figured by the month.

sections.h2: What happens to taxes and excise tax when you sell in Adams County?
sections.html:
The property tax lien runs from January 1, and unless the sale contract says otherwise, the seller owes the share of that year's tax for the days before the sale and the buyer owes the rest (RCW 84.60.020). Most contracts and escrow instructions settle this directly, so read yours.

Every transfer also needs a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit filed with the Treasurer before the deed is recorded at the Auditor. The county will not accept an incomplete affidavit, and forms must be on legal-size paper (8.5 by 14 inches).

  • Excise tax is due within 30 days of the sale date, and the Department of Revenue treats the notarized deed date as the date of sale.
  • The county adds a local 0.25 percent of the price plus a $5 processing fee to the state portion.
  • The state rate is graduated: 1.1 percent on the first slice, then 1.28, 2.75 and 3.0 percent. For sales starting January 1, 2027 the breakpoints are $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000.
  • Land classified as agricultural or timberland pays a flat 1.28 percent state rate if the buyer will keep using it that way and the Assessor signs the Notice of Continuance on the affidavit.

That last rule matters in a county built on farmland. Sellers of wheat ground or irrigated parcels should call the Assessor before the closing date, not after.

sections.h2: How do you challenge an assessed value in Adams County?
sections.html:
You petition the county board of equalization on a Department of Revenue form. Under RCW 84.40.038 the petition is due by July 1 of the assessment year, within 30 days after the notice was mailed or sent electronically, or within a county-adopted limit of up to 60 days, whichever is latest.

The board may waive a late filing when the petition arrives within a reasonable time and the owner shows good cause. Listed causes include a death or serious illness in the immediate family, incorrect written advice from assessor or board staff, a natural disaster, and postal delay documented by the Postal Service. Call the Assessor at 509-659-3200 to learn which deadline your notice carries. The board decides the value only, and the dollar tax levied by each district cannot be appealed.

sections.h2: What property tax relief exists in Adams County?
sections.html:
The county lists a senior citizen and disability exemption, and the Assessor is the office to call about it. According to the county page, applicants must be at least 61 years old on December 31 of the application year, the home must be the principal residence on up to one acre, and household income must be $41,000 or less.

  • State law at RCW 84.36.381 also admits people retired because of disability and veterans receiving VA compensation at a service-connected rating of 40 percent or higher.
  • A person who sells or is displaced from a home can transfer exemption status to a replacement residence, though no one may claim it on more than one home in a year.
  • Tax statements carry a notice about the state deferral program in chapter 84.38 RCW.
  • For help with a mortgage or tax problem, the Washington Homeownership Resource Center answers at 877-894-4663.

sections.h2: What happens when Adams County taxes go unpaid for three years?
sections.html:
The Treasurer starts foreclosure. In July the Certificate of Delinquency is filed with Adams County Superior Court, foreclosure costs begin to accrue, and a title search is run on each parcel. Everyone with a recorded interest is served by certified mail, and the notice is also published in the county's official newspaper.

  • The court enters a judgment foreclosing the tax lien and authorizing a public auction.
  • Owners and others with a legal interest can redeem until the close of business the day before the sale.
  • Parcels that do not sell become Tax Title Property held in trust by the county, and a list is available by emailing the Treasurer.
  • A certificate of delinquency cannot be filed when the delinquent tax is $100 or less, excluding interest and penalties (RCW 84.64.050).

Personal property is handled differently: the treasurer is directed to seize and sell it once those taxes turn delinquent.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Adams County, WA?
faqs.a: Full payment is due April 30, or half by April 30 and half by October 31 when the bill is over $50. The 2026 second half was due October 31, 2026, so anything unpaid from that installment is now delinquent and accrues interest by the month.

faqs.q: What is the interest rate on late taxes in Adams County?
faqs.a: For a residence with four or fewer units the rate is 9 percent a year with no penalties. Other property pays 12 percent a year plus a 3 percent penalty on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1. Both come from RCW 84.56.020.

faqs.q: Who pays real estate excise tax when I sell in Adams County?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays, and the buyer becomes responsible if the seller does not. The Treasurer collects it with the affidavit before the Auditor records the deed. The local share is 0.25 percent of the sale price, with a $5 processing fee.

faqs.q: How long does Adams County wait before foreclosing for unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Three full years. After that the Treasurer files a Certificate of Delinquency with the Superior Court in July, and the owner can redeem until the close of business the day before the auction.

faqs.q: Who can I call about the senior exemption in Adams County?
faqs.a: Call the Adams County Assessor's Office at 509-659-3200. The county page lists a minimum age of 61 by December 31 of the application year, a principal residence on up to one acre, and an income limit of $41,000.
